statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-106069 is a Node.js TLS hostname-verification flaw: tls.checkServerIdentity() can validate a certificate against a different IP address than the one connected to when the host is a non-canonical IPv4 literal with a leading zero, such as 0127.0.0.1. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.23.4, the 2026-10-21 security release (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases), with commit d7663560ac, 'tls: reject non-canonical IP addresses' (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/d7663560ac), which carries this CVE id. Release notes: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.4. The flaw needs the host to be normalized with domainToASCII() before it is matched, which 22.x first does in 22.23.0, with commit 2197a47144, 'tls: normalize hostname for server identity checks' (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/2197a47144); 22.22.x matches the host as written, so it never reads 0127.0.0.1 as 87.0.0.1. We read the node binary in every published DHI nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64: 22.23.4-r0 is the first that reports Node.js v22.23.4 and contains the 'Host is a non-canonical IP address' rejection this commit adds to tls.checkServerIdentity(); 22.22.0-r0 through 22.23.3-r0 report Node.js 22.22.0 through 22.23.3 and lack it. We also called tls.checkServerIdentity('0127.0.0.1') with a certificate whose only SAN is IP Address:87.0.0.1 on the aarch64 builds: 22.23.0-r0 accepts it, the 22.22.0-r0 and 22.22.3-r0 builds reject it because it does not treat the host as an IP address, and 22.23.4-r0 rejects it as a non-canonical IP address. The range therefore starts at 22.23.0-r0.

CVE-2026-106069: tls.checkServerIdentity() normalizes a leading-zero IPv4 literal such as 0127.0.0.1 differently from the system resolver, so the certificate can be checked against a different IP address than the one connected to. Node.js fixed it on the 24.x line in 24.22.1, the October 2026 security release (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases, https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v24.22.1), with https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/935918e342 (tls: reject non-canonical IP addresses). We read the version string from the node binary in every published nodejs-24 package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (24.13.0-r0 to the current 24.22.3-r0, x86_64 and aarch64); each matches its package version, so builds below 24.22.1-r0 ship Node.js 24.22.0 or older and 24.22.1-r0 and every later build ship 24.22.1 or newer. The range ends at 24.22.1-r0, the first fixed build.
